channel.title: Earning Money Online UK
channel.description: Practical UK money guides with real figures, honest maths and named sources. Make money, save money, side hustles, careers and buying decisions.

item.title: The water tariff that is cheaper until it suddenly is not, and where the line sits
item.description: Severn Trent's Water Smart trial charges three rates by monthly use. On 2026/27 rates it is cheaper up to about 12.5 cubic metres a month, then dearer, fast.

item.title: A washer dryer label carries two of everything, and most people read the wrong half
item.description: A washer dryer label shows two of everything by law, including two capacities. Read the complete cycle column first, then see the real running cost gap.

item.title: There is a line on your water bill for taking away rain that may never reach a sewer
item.description: If all your rainwater goes to a soakaway, the surface water drainage charge can go, up to £73.44 a year, backdated six years. What it is worth, and the trap.

item.title: Self Assessment payment on 31 January 2027: how much will you pay, and can you cut it?
item.description: Your 31 January 2027 Self Assessment payment can be your tax bill plus a first payment on account. Here is the sum, the 8.00% interest rate and how to cut it.

item.title: The most expensive thing in your house is probably a toilet you cannot hear
item.description: A leaking toilet can waste up to 400 litres a day, Severn Trent says. At 2026/27 metered rates that is about £598 a year. The sums, and the free five minute test.

item.title: Heating oil nearly doubled in a single month this year, and the usual advice did not protect anyone
item.description: UK heating oil went from 53p a litre in February 2026 to 104p in March, then 90p by August. What the official figures mean for when you order your next fill.

item.title: Your washing machine's label describes one programme, and it is not the one you press
item.description: Eco 40-60 is the only wash programme your energy label measures, averaged over three load sizes. At 26.32p a kWh, see what pressing eco saves you a year.

item.title: Deposit deductions and fair wear and tear: what a landlord can actually keep
item.description: A landlord can only deduct for damage beyond fair wear and tear. The 5 week deposit cap, the free dispute service, and up to 3 times the deposit if unprotected.

item.title: Artificial grass is sold as a saving, and there is almost nothing there to save
item.description: Artificial grass costs about £50 to £90 a square metre fitted, while a real lawn costs £10 to £80 a year to run. The payback, worked out at November 2026 rates.

item.title: Skilled Worker Visa and Modern Slavery: What the 3 September Rule Change Really Does
item.description: From 8 October 2026 the Home Office lifts the sponsor tie for Skilled Worker visa holders recognised as modern slavery victims. What the rule actually requires, the Conclusive Grounds decision you need first, and how long that really takes.

item.title: Most People Buy Zapier Before They Need It. Here Is How To Tell When You Actually Do
item.description: Zapier's free tier gives you 100 tasks a month, and filters, Formatter and Paths do not use any of them. Which three jobs in a one person UK business are worth automating first, which one never is, and how to tell before you pay.

item.title: Working age benefits went up 3.8%. Pensioners got 4.8%. Here is why
item.description: Working age benefits rose by CPI at 3.8% for the year ending March 2027. Pensioners got 4.8%. Universal Credit got more than both. Here is what each actually means.

item.title: Winter Fuel Payment claims open on Monday, and the £35,000 rule is not what most people think
item.description: Claims for winter 2026 to 2027 open on 21 September 2026. You could get £100 to £300, but income over £35,000 means HMRC takes it back. Here is how the rule actually works.

item.title: The £150 Warm Home Discount was already decided, on a date in August nobody announced
item.description: The Warm Home Discount is a £150 discount off your electricity bill, mostly awarded automatically. The qualifying date for winter 2026/27 was 23 August 2026, and it has passed.

item.title: One Rule Decides This, and It Is Not the One in the Headline
item.description: The VAT Flat Rate Scheme runs to £150,000, not £90,000. Flat rate against standard VAT on £100,000 of sales, with the 16.5% limited cost trap and every break-even figure.

item.title: The Twitch Affiliate Bar Halved And Nobody Updated Their Guide
item.description: Twitch's own help page now lists four Affiliate requirements: 25 followers, 4 hours streamed, 4 different days and an average of 3 viewers. The old 50 followers and 500 minutes figures are everywhere and they are wrong. What Affiliate and Partner actually give you, and the split Twitch will not print.

item.title: £20.50 a Year to Keep Your Own Name, or Several Thousand to Change It
item.description: A UK trade mark costs £205 online for one class plus £60 a class, and lasts 10 years. Right Start costs more, not less. Full fee table, the classes trap, and the rebrand cost you are insuring against.

item.title: Four Letters On Your Payslip Decide Whether You Are Overpaying Tax
item.description: A tax code ending W1, M1, X or NONCUM is an emergency code, and HMRC says it can take up to 35 days from starting a job to fix. What the letters mean, what a P800 is, and the one case where an emergency code is completely normal and you should leave it alone.

item.title: How Many Paying Subscribers You Actually Need, On British Card Fees Rather Than American Ones
item.description: Substack takes 10%. The card fee every guide quotes is Stripe's US rate. Stripe's published UK rate is 1.5% plus 20p on standard UK cards, which changes the answer. How many subscribers you need at £3, £5 and £8 a month, and why annual billing saves eleven fixed fees.

item.title: The Subscription Is the Smallest Number in This Decision
item.description: Ecommerce platform costs compared over three years on £60,000 of annual sales, including the extra transaction fee, hosting, apps and your own time, with cost per £1,000 of sales.

item.title: September CPI came in at 3.5%: here is what it did to your April 2027 benefits
item.description: September 2026 CPI came in at 3.5%. Most benefits rise 3.5% in April 2027, the State Pension 3.9% and Universal Credit more. Here is what you will get.

item.title: Two Ways to Pay for the Same Commute, and One Is Better Even If You Have the Cash
item.description: An interest-free employer season ticket loan under £10,000 is tax-free under HMRC beneficial loan rules. Priced against monthly tickets and against paying cash at a 3.75% Bank Rate.

item.title: They Do Not Have To Tell You The Salary. They Do Have To Tell You Something Else
item.description: There is no UK law requiring a salary band in a job advert. But any employer with 250 or more staff must publish gender pay gap data, and it is searchable free on a government service. How to use the data that does exist when the band you want does not.

item.title: One of These Insurances Is Compulsory and It Is Not the One You Think
item.description: Public liability insurance is voluntary in the UK. Employers’ liability is compulsory at £5 million. Here is who actually forces you to buy cover, priced per activity with the break-even in jobs.

item.title: The Law Does Not Make You Buy This. Your Client’s Contract Does
item.description: Professional indemnity is not legally required for most UK freelancers. It is claims-made, which changes everything. What it covers, what it does not, and how to price it against your own day rate.

item.title: Every pension scheme must connect by 31 October. You still will not be able to use a dashboard
item.description: Every relevant pension scheme must connect to the dashboards ecosystem by 31 October 2026. That is not the date you can use a dashboard. Here is the difference, and why it matters.

item.title: A Quarter of Your Pension for an Afternoon of Letters
item.description: The Pension Tracing Service is free but only gives contact details, not valuations. Compared against commercial tracers charging 5% to 25% of the pot, with the break-even in hours of your time.

item.title: One Route Makes Your Donation Cheaper. The Other Makes It Bigger. They Are Not The Same Choice
item.description: To give a charity £1 through Payroll Giving you pay 80p at basic rate and 60p at higher rate. Through Gift Aid you pay the full £1 and claim back later. Which leaves the charity better off, which leaves you better off, and why they are not the same answer.

item.title: Three Members At £10 Beat Ten Members At £3, And It Is Not Close
item.description: Patreon's pricing page says 10%, then adds payment processing, currency conversion and payout fees without printing a rate for any of them. What that means for a UK creator, why tier design beats audience size, and the number of members you actually need.

item.title: Your Employer Pays 25p. HMRC Says 55p. The Difference Is Yours to Claim
item.description: HMRC approves 55p a mile for the first 10,000 business miles in 2026/27. If your employer pays less you can claim relief on the shortfall, and backdate it four years. Full value table.
